Thanks again for the call this morning — great conversation and helpful context on Acme's latency-sensitive search use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps below.

Recap (high level)
- Primary goal: reduce inference cost and tail latency for near-real-time search ranking across US/EU users.
- Workloads: mixed short chat-style queries + long-form reranking during batch reindex.
- Success metrics: P95 latency < 200ms for the online path; cost per 1M tokens target discussed.

Proposed next step
- Technical deep-dive + demo (45–60 min) to show a live run of the model pipeline, KV cache behavior, and routing/fallback config.

Scheduling suggestion (to reduce travel/odd-hour burden we recommend rotating the weekly meeting time across regions):
- Week A (US-friendly): Tue 10:00 AM ET / 07:00 AM PT / Tue 15:00 CET
- Week B (EU-friendly): Wed 03:00 PM CET / Wed 09:00 AM ET / Wed 18:00 PM SGT
- Week C (APAC-friendly): Thu 10:00 AM SGT / Thu 03:00 AM ET (early) / Thu 00:00 AM PT

Rotation cadence idea: repeat a 3-week rotation so the meeting alternates each week between US/EU/APAC-friendly windows. That way no single team is always on at an inconvenient hour.

Please pick two preferred slots from the examples above (one primary, one backup) or propose times that work better for your lead engineers. I can lock a rotating recurrence and send calendar invites (ICS) that rotate the meeting time weekly.

Attachments: discovery-notes.pdf (call notes + initial requirements).
Calendar link: https://cal.link/rotate-demo (pick a time and it will surface our rotating options).

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.
